question: Do current taxonomic authorities reconcile the two name groups in the 14 candidate FishNet2/KAUM catalog-number pairs without overstating specimen identity, locality, or reuse?

worms.provider: World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS), Aphia REST API
worms.responseStatus: All six exact-name requests returned HTTP 200 with one exact-name record each.
worms.interpretation: WoRMS accepted-name links support a nomenclatural crosswalk only; they do not validate any collection specimen or occurrence row.

catalogOfFishes.provider: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
catalogOfFishes.interpretation: The exact Jaydia poeciloptera and Ostorhinchus pleuron catalog records report those current valid usages. The Jaydia poecilopterus exact-combination query returned no records; the poeciloptera record notes historical literature using that combination but gives current status as Jaydia poeciloptera.

method.candidatePairingLimit: The source-row pairs are inherited from the separate GBIF candidate crosswalk and still carry institution/collection quality flags. Taxonomic agreement cannot upgrade a candidate row-pair to curator confirmation.

sourceCitation: WoRMS Editorial Board (2026), Aphia REST name records accessed 2026-11-21; Fricke, R., Eschmeyer, W. N. & Van der Laan, R. (eds.) (2026), Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences, records accessed 2026-11-21.

nameCrosswalks.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Jaydia poeciloptera (Cuvier, 1828). The record also documents historical usages of Jaydia poecilopterus and Ostorhinchus poecilopterus.
nameCrosswalks.decision: A supported nomenclatural crosswalk to Jaydia poeciloptera; preserve all three source and GBIF name strings in provenance.

nameCrosswalks.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Ostorhinchus pleuron (Fraser, 2005).
nameCrosswalks.decision: The original Apogon combination maps nomenclaturally to Ostorhinchus pleuron; preserve both strings in provenance.

limitations: This review reconciles names only. It does not re-identify any fish or verify specimen images, vouchers, or museum labels.
The 14 source-row pairs remain candidates because the separate GBIF rows carry INSTITUTION_MATCH_FUZZY and INSTITUTION_COLLECTION_MISMATCH flags and no curator confirmation was obtained.

The separate KAUM GBIF candidate data reports locality as off Rosario, Cavite; it does not assign any fish to Cañas River. The FishNet2 export itself lacks a locality string, event date, coordinate uncertainty, and explicit datum for these rows.
FishNet2 redistribution permission remains unresolved despite the separate KAUM dataset's CC-BY 4.0 metadata. No public reuse is approved.
Taxonomic name status does not establish current local presence, habitat use at a specific waterbody, abundance, safety, catchability, fishing access, diet, or bait advice.
decision: Retain both current-name crosswalks in research metadata while preserving verbatim FishNet2, KAUM-source, and GBIF-interpreted labels. Do not create a Cañas River or Cavite presence assertion, add app species rows, or project the candidate pairs publicly until record identity, locality, and reuse questions are independently resolved.
followUps: Seek a curator-confirmed mapping from the KAUM/NMNS collection source for catalog numbers 57150-57163, if access becomes available.
Clarify whether FishNet2 portal restrictions apply to these records in the OBIS mirror and obtain any required redistribution consent before public reuse.
Keep the candidate source locality off Rosario separate from Cañas River and from any named Cavite fishing-waterbody assignment.
